title: Nuclear Radius from Coulomb Energy
q_prose: The electrostatic energy of Z protons in a spherical nucleus of radius R is given below. Given the measured masses of the neutron, hydrogen, N-15 and O-15, and that their binding-energy difference is purely electrostatic, find the nuclear radius.
q_reminder: Find R  ·  binding-energy difference of  N-15  and  O-15  is purely electrostatic
q_narration: Here is a beautiful JEE Advanced 2016 problem from nuclear physics. The electrostatic energy of Z protons in a nucleus of radius R is three-fifths, Z times Z minus one, e squared, over four pi epsilon-nought R. We are given the masses of the neutron, hydrogen, nitrogen fifteen and oxygen fifteen, and told the difference in their binding energies is purely electrostatic. Find the radius. Let us solve it, step by step.

steps.label: Step 1 — Mirror nuclei
steps.narration: Step one. Nitrogen fifteen has seven protons; oxygen fifteen has eight. These are mirror nuclei, with protons and neutrons swapped, and we are told their radii are equal. So the only thing that differs between them is the electrostatic energy of the protons.

steps.label: Step 2 — Coulomb energy difference
steps.narration: Step two. Put each Z into the energy formula and subtract. Eight times seven is fifty-six; seven times six is forty-two; the difference is fourteen. And three-fifths of fourteen is eight point four. So the Coulomb energy difference is eight point four times e squared over four pi epsilon-nought R.

steps.label: Step 3 — Energy difference from masses
steps.narration: Step three. That same energy difference appears as a difference in mass. Oxygen minus nitrogen, plus neutron minus hydrogen, gives zero point zero zero three seven nine six atomic mass units. Multiply by nine hundred thirty-one point five, and the energy difference is three point five three six mega electron volts.

steps.label: Step 4 — Solve for R
steps.narration: Step four. Now solve for R. Using e squared over four pi epsilon-nought equals one point four four mega electron volt femtometre, R equals eight point four times one point four four, divided by three point five three six. That gives three point four two femtometres.
